objectives.outcome: the learner can read aloud and write in figures whole numbers up to 10,000, matching words to numerals.
external_prerequisites: Grade 3 numbers to 1,000 (assumed prior; not a pilot objective)

objectives.outcome: the learner can state the value of each digit in a number up to 100,000 (ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones).
the learner can compare and order whole numbers to 100,000 using >, <, =.
the learner can round whole numbers to the nearest 10 and 100.
the learner can add two 4-digit numbers, carrying across places.
the learner can subtract 4-digit numbers with regrouping (borrowing), including across a zero.
the learner can choose add or subtract for one- and two-step everyday word problems and solve them.
the learner can estimate sums/differences by rounding and check whether an answer is reasonable.
the learner can recall multiplication facts to 10×10 and explain multiplication as repeated addition / equal groups.
the learner can multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number with regrouping.
the learner can multiply 3-digit by 1-digit and 2-digit by 2-digit numbers using the standard method.
the learner can identify and solve multiplication word problems (equal groups, arrays, rate).
the learner can explain division as equal sharing / equal grouping and relate it to multiplication.
the learner can divide within known facts and express what is left over as a remainder.
the learner can divide a 2–3 digit number by a 1-digit number using the standard method, with remainders.
the learner can solve division word problems and interpret the remainder in context.
the learner can name a fraction as an equal part of a whole (halves, quarters).
the learner can read and write a fraction and identify what the top and bottom numbers mean, including thirds, fifths, and eighths.
the learner can find simple equivalent fractions (e.g. 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6).
the learner can compare two fractions with the same denominator, and simple unit fractions.
the learner can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator.
the learner can measure length and convert between metres and centimetres (1 m = 100 cm).
the learner can compare and convert mass between kilograms and grams (1 kg = 1000 g).
the learner can compare and convert capacity between litres and millilitres (1 l = 1000 ml).
the learner can read time on analogue and digital clocks (to 5 minutes) and use days/weeks/months.
the learner can identify and name lines, rays, and line segments.
the learner can recognize right, acute, and obtuse angles.
the learner can name common 2D shapes and state sides/corners (triangle, square, rectangle, circle).
the learner can identify one or more lines of symmetry in simple shapes and patterns.
the learner can read a pictograph where one symbol stands for a fixed number.
the learner can read a bar graph with a scale and compare categories.
